Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

vote noun and verb

also votes, voting, voter, cast a vote, vote for, ballot, ballot paper, secret ballot, ballot box, take a vote, the right to vote, call for a vote, a vote was taken

classical

Cic. Fam. 11.27.7: ego tē suffrāgium tulisse in illā lēge prīmum nōn crēdidī
Traupman 181: suffrāgium ferō, vote
M-O s.v. vote vb.; vote: ballot
Traupman 178

suffrāgium, suffrāgiī n.

noun, second declension

a vote; the right to vote

To vote is suffrāgium ferre (Cic., Varro; Traupman 181; M-O). Lewis & Short: a voting tablet, a vote, and the right of voting; Morgan–Owens adds jūs suffrāgiī for the right to vote. A Roman citizen voted in his century or tribe at the comitia (see election).

Other words

  • suffrāgor, suffrāgārī, suffrāgātus sum — vote for; support

    verb, first conjugation, deponent, with the dative · also used · classical · Cic. Mur. 71 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 181: vote for

    Of voters and, by extension, of anyone who backs a person or a cause (Lewis & Short).

  • tabella, tabellae f. — a ballot: the voting tablet

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 3.39: habeat sānē populus tabellam quasi vindicem lībertātis; Traupman 178: ballot; M-O s.v. vote: ballot

    The tablet of the secret ballot, brought in by the four lēgēs tabellāriae (Cic. Leg. 3.35). A ballot box is urna, the Roman voting urn (Lewis & Short; M-O), or Traupman’s suffrāgiōrum cista (Traupman 178).

  • sententia, sententiae f. — a senator’s vote: the opinion he states when asked

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 181: discessiō facta est in ejus sententiam, a vote was taken on his motion

    Senators did not cast ballots: each gave his sententia when asked, and the house then divided by walking to one side (discessiō, below). Traupman gives cēnseō for a senator’s vote (Traupman 181).

  • discessiō, discessiōnis f. — a division of the house: a vote taken by people moving to one side

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sest. 74: fieretque sine ūllā varietāte discessiō; Traupman 181: discessiōnem faciō, call for a vote

    To put a motion to the vote this way is discessiōnem facere (Lewis & Short).

  • suffrāgiōrum cista — ballot box

    also used · modern · Traupman 178

Examples

  • ego tē suffrāgium tulisse in illā lēge prīmum nōn crēdidī

    to begin with, I didn’t believe you had voted on that lawCic. Fam. 11.27.7

  • omnēs comitiōrum diē tabellās postulāvērunt

    on election day they all asked for ballotsPlin. Ep. 3.20.2

  • habeat sānē populus tabellam quasi vindicem lībertātis

    by all means let the people have the secret ballot, as the guardian of its freedomCic. Leg. 3.39

  • discessiōnem facere

    to call for a vote (in the senate)Traupman 181

  • discessiō facta est in ejus sententiam

    a vote was taken on his motionTraupman 181

See also election, political, law, office.
